Senses.Explanation: To appraise, sort out, or distinguish; noun constructions name the resulting appraisal or classificatory distinction. The term is attested 266 times in 126 allowlisted texts. A monk sets two episodes side by side and asks the teacher to “please appraise and distinguish” them (兩段不同，試請料揀); another record asks who can sort out a presented conjunction. The same appraisal vocabulary appears in Linji's “Four Selections” (四料揀). The Record of the Eyes of Humans and Gods asks, “the Four Selections—what do the selections select?” (四料揀，料揀何法), and another exposition begins with people of middle and lower capacity under that heading. A later record calls paired evaluative formulas “the old so-called selection sayings” (古所謂料揀語). The public act, resulting distinction, and named set remain one appraisal-and-selection family; noun and verb grammar alone do not create different lexical things.
Senses.Note: The former action/result targets were not independently distinguishable from their glosses. The standalone word remains compatible with the separate named Four Selections article and its four formulations. The Chan deviation is public appraisal of sayings, encounters, and speakers, plus its use in Linji classificatory vocabulary.

AlternateTargets: Xiangyan's man in the tree case
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘Xiangyan up a tree.’ The phrase occurs 119 times in 72 allowlisted texts and names a public case. Xiangyan poses a man in a tree whose mouth grips a branch while his hands grasp no branch and his feet stand on none. Someone below asks the meaning of the ancestral teacher's coming from the west: not answering violates the question, while answering costs his life. Later records preserve Hutou's counter-question, ‘leave being up the tree aside; please speak before he climbed the tree’; masters question monks on the case in entering interviews, strike one who walks away, and answer renewed public questions with such replies as ‘Heaven! Heaven!’ The headword names this stable case and its testing history; it does not denote Xiangyan as a dictionary figure apart from the case.
Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary climbing scene into a named public-interview record whose demand to answer is explicit in the Chinese. Xiangyan is a lineage master and stays on the roster. The man in the scenario and the case title remain one case referent, not separate senses.
